name: the Brooklyn Botanic Garden
title: Ancient Trees in the Brooklyn Botanic Garden: 5 to Find
meta_description: The largest Kansas hawthorn in the United States, a wingnut on a crutch and a pawpaw on New York's Great Trees list. Five trees in Brooklyn Botanic Garden.
intro: The largest Kansas hawthorn in the United States grows beside the Lily Pool in Brooklyn, a species that normally gives up at around twenty feet. This one reached 35 and was named a national champion in 1985. Rochester's parks department sent it in 1912. A Caucasian wingnut north of the Rock Garden came from Rome in 1922, and the garden props and cables its lower limbs so they do not tear from a trunk it calls nearly nine feet through. Three more have been on New York City's Great Trees list since its first edition in 1985, and the list is generous with size. A pawpaw in the Plant Family Collection has a trunk of only ten inches, and a Chinese parasol tree that the US National Arboretum posted to Brooklyn in 1971 made the list fourteen years later. A mountain winterberry, a holly, on the south side of the Rock Garden was measured at about 2.2 metres round.
